$comment: The acceptance questionnaire (ADR-0074, F-027-i) — the declared home of the
16 row keys, their scope and what an unmet answer costs.
These strings cross a process boundary: network-service writes them into
network.panel.capabilities as JSONB, and the panel's systems page reads them
back to render the capability matrix and the registration refusal (F-027-ad).
No import joins Go and TypeScript, so this fixture plus a test on each side
replaces one (ADR-0036, C-04). The Go half is
severity: required = the panel is refused at registration; metered = accepted
but may not sell metered service (ADR-0072); degrades = accepted, and the
system does something else rather than guess.
scope: which transports answer the row. A row outside a panel's scope is not

rows.question: Does it report a usage figure for one named client, rather than only a server total?
rows.unmet: Refused: a server total cannot be split between the users on it, so there is nothing to bill (ADR-0074, revisit trigger).

rows.question: Does one call return the usage of every client on the panel?
rows.unmet: Refused: 5000 clients would be 5000 requests a pass on someone else's server (catalog 8.4, F-027-k).

rows.question: Does one call return the usage of a named subset of clients?
rows.unmet: The hot loop re-reads the whole panel each pass, so its interval is bounded by the cost of the bulk call (F-027-u).

rows.question: Can a client's counter be zeroed on request?
rows.unmet: Nothing is lost: we only ever read a counter. A reset is something we detect, never something we cause (F-027-l).

rows.question: Does a client's counter keep its value when the client is updated — a ceiling written, a label changed?
rows.unmet: Every ceiling write looks like a reset, so the cursor is re-read in the same pass as the write instead of at the next one (ADR-0072, F-027-t).

rows.question: Does the NAS send Acct-Input-Gigawords and Acct-Output-Gigawords beside the 32-bit octet counters?
rows.unmet: A session past 4 GB is held rather than billed, and never extrapolated (invariant 29, ADR-0074).

rows.question: Can a byte ceiling be written for one client, and does the panel enforce it itself?
rows.unmet: No metered sale: the ceiling is the only enforcement point that still works while our service is down, and without it no byte can be paid for before it is served (ADR-0072).

rows.question: Does the enforced ceiling count the same bytes the usage figure reports — both directions, same units?
rows.unmet: No metered sale: a block bought against the cursor would be spent against a different number, and the gap is free traffic with nothing red anywhere.

rows.question: Can a bandwidth rate be written for one client?
rows.unmet: A custom rate rule is recorded and not enforced at the far end; layer-1 limiting stays ours.

rows.question: Can one client be disabled and re-enabled without deleting it?
rows.unmet: Refused: suspension would have to delete the client, and a top-up could then not restore it (ADR-0075, F-027-x).

rows.question: Can a client be created, updated and deleted through the API?
rows.unmet: Refused: nothing can be provisioned or purged, so desired state has nothing to converge on (F-027-z).

rows.question: Does a client carry an id that survives being renamed?
rows.unmet: Matching falls through to the claim tag and then the uuid, so a rename reads as missing until the second key is tried (F-027-aa).

rows.question: Can we store our own claim tag on the client — a note, label or remark field we own?
rows.unmet: The second matching key does not exist here, so a client rebuilt on the far end reads as an orphan rather than as ours (F-027-aa).

rows.question: Does the panel serve a subscription URL for a client?
rows.unmet: The link is built from the inbound by BuildLink, so an inbound change reaches the user only when the link is fetched again.

rows.question: Does the panel enforce an expiry date on a client by itself?
rows.unmet: Expiry is ours alone: a Grant that ends while our loop is down leaves the client carrying traffic until the loop returns.

rows.question: Can the panel's own billing or credit be switched off, leaving us the only writer of the quota?
rows.unmet: The panel cuts users off on a schedule we do not control, so it is run metering_only and the tenant keeps its own billing (F-027-ay).
